svg.text: Глава 7 · Кодирование и мультиплексирование данных
Олифер, 7-е изд. · RAG p0215:c01–p0241:c01 · PDF 215–241 · printed 214–240
1 · Coding criteria
Discrete/analog information × discrete/analog signal → four conversion classes
Signal spectrum must fit the line's passband
Receiver needs timing/self-synchronization
Noise tolerance and error detection/correction matter
Transmitter power is also part of code-selection trade-off
No single line code optimizes all properties simultaneously
2 · Discrete line codes
NRZ → simple / narrow spectrum, but long-run sync/DC problems
AMI / NRZI → use transitions/polarity to improve properties
Manchester → strong self-sync, wider spectrum
4B/5B / 64B/66B → redundant block coding
B8ZS / HDB3 / scrambling → avoid problematic zero runs
3 · Analog modulation for data
ASK → amplitude · FSK → frequency · PSK → phase
BPSK/QPSK → phase states carry one/multiple bits
QAM → combine amplitude + phase; constellation states represent bit groups
I/Q → in-phase + quadrature components implement mod/demod
More states improve bits/symbol but require better discrimination under noise
4 · Error control
Parity → cheap, low diagnostic power
CRC/FCS → stronger frame error detection with low relative overhead
FEC → enough redundancy to correct without retransmission
Hamming distance → codeword separation and correction capability
Convolutional codes → source example for burst-error environments
5 · Analog information digitization
Analog→analog → AM/FM shift information into another spectral region
Analog→digital → sample in time + quantize amplitude
ADC produces binary samples · DAC reconstructs the waveform
Sampling theorem constrains sample rate relative to source spectrum
PCM source example → voice sampled at 8 kHz into 7/8-bit values
6 · Multiplexing and switching
FDM → fixed frequency bands per channel
WDM/CWDM/DWDM → analogous spectral split in optical domain
Asynchronous TDM → packet-time sharing in source taxonomy
Synchronous TDM → recurring slot for every flow in each cycle
Slot position = channel identity; switch reorders slot/byte positions
Operational reading rule
Do not debug “bandwidth” without identifying line code/modulation, symbol rate, spectrum and clock recovery.
Do not confuse error detection with correction; do not confuse synchronous time-slot identity with packet addressing.
No executable CLI is supplied by the chapter.
Chapter 8 starts at p0242:c01 · reading state unchanged · extraction findings recorded separately.
